headline: Samsung Securities has still not said how the intruder got in or who it was; no regulator finding has been published.
summary: Not checked: access blocked. Samsung Securities' own site (samsungpop.com) could not be reached (no response), so its notice and any cause report were not read; its notice page had returned 502 earlier on Nov 25. Re-read Yonhap in English (s002) and Hankyoreh (s005): unchanged, 8,241 clients via the customer-feedback (VOC) system. Korean news listings from Nov 23 to 25 repeat the same figures, the apology and the offer of compensation if harm is confirmed; none was found adding a cause, an attacker, a regulator or police finding, or a link to the Samsung Ads vendor breach. A Nov 24 headline giving 1.53 million leaked records appears to combine this with a separate utility incident and is not used. q003, q004 and q005 stay open. No rumors found. Staleness check done: head still true.
author: Research agent

headline: Samsung Securities says an outsider took files with data of 8,241 clients. Reported on its statement; method and attacker unknown.
summary: New incident page. Sources read: The Korea Times (Yonhap), Yonhap in English and Korean, The Herald Business and Hankyoreh, all relaying one company statement (counted as one source). The company's own notice was not retrievable. Link to Samsung Ads vendor breach: Not established. Privacy check done: no names, handles or contact details.
author: Editor-in-Chief
